question: There are 50 students in a class. If the average weight of 39 students is 32 kg and the average weight of the entire class is 34 kg, then what is the average weight (in kg) of rest of the 11 students of the class? (Correct up to two decimal places)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total deviation of 39 students from the overall average = 39 × (32 − 34) = −78 kg.

To maintain the overall average, the remaining 11 students must balance this with an opposite deviation of +78 kg.

Average deviation for these 11 students = +78 ÷ 11 ≈ +7.09 kg.

Required average of the 11 students = Overall Average + Deviation = 34 + 7.09 = 41.09 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 41.09 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of students = 50

Overall average weight of the class = 34 kg

Average weight of 39 students = 32 kg

Number of remaining students = 50 − 39 = 11

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

 Total: 50 Students | Overall Avg: 34 kg
 
 
 
 39 Students
 Avg Weight: 32 kg

 
 
 11 Students
 Avg: ?

 
 Total Weight = 50 × 34 = 1700 kg
 Part 1 Weight = 39 × 32 = 1248 kg
 Remaining Weight = 1700 − 1248 = 452 kg

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of all 50 students = 50 × 34 = 1700 kg

⇒ Total weight of 39 students = 39 × 32 = 1248 kg

⇒ Total weight of the remaining 11 students = 1700 − 1248 = 452 kg

⇒ Average weight of the remaining 11 students = 452 ÷ 11

⇒ Average weight = 41.0909... ≈ 41.09 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 41.09 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

Used when combining groups of different sizes to find the central value. Formula: Aw = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Deviation Method

The net sum of deviations of all elements from their mean is always zero. This property provides a highly effective shortcut for finding missing values in a group.

Replacement Concept in Averages

When a new member replaces an existing one, the change in the total sum equals the difference in their values. New Value = Old Value + (Total Members × Change in Average).
